candidates.attacker_control: An authenticated caller controls (a) the request path (/v2/workflow-instances, /v2/workflows/query, /v2/tasks/query, /v2/schedules/filter), (b) the JSON body, in particular whether `projectName` is present, and (c) any other filter values (name, state, host, start/end time). Session cookie `sessionId` or the `token` header is required, but any enabled account (UserType.GENERAL_USER with zero project grants) can obtain one; no admin role is needed.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that the check itself is effective when invoked (ProjectServiceImpl.checkProjectAndAuthThrowException throws on missing project permission); v1 endpoints always carry projectCode in the path and call the check, so the omission is v2-specific rather than a repository-wide convention; confirmed the interceptor chain (AppConfiguration.addInterceptors) has no admin/role gate for /v2/**; confirmed there is no @PreAuthorize/RequiresPermissions usage; confirmed the get-by-id v2 methods (getTaskDefinition, getProcessDefinition, getSchedule) do resolve the project and check permissions, so only the filter/list methods lack it; confirmed the DTOs allow an empty body with default paging; confirmed the mapper queries have no user/project-relation join that would implicitly restrict rows.
candidates.impact: Cross-project (cross-tenant) confidentiality breach over the network using a normal authenticated account: disclosure of workflow definitions (global parameters/locations may include credentials or business data), task definitions and parameters, schedules (crontab), and workflow instance metadata (hosts, executors, states, times) for every project in the deployment. The leaked codes/names also enable follow-on targeting of further v2 endpoints. No code execution or data modification is demonstrated; impact is information disclosure/authorization bypass.
candidates.prerequisites: API server reachable and a valid session/API token for any enabled user (including a user with no project permissions). The v2 controllers are part of the default api-server module and are not conditionally disabled in source; pageNo/pageSize have defaults, so an empty JSON body is sufficient.
candidates.root_cause: In the v2 service methods, the project permission check is conditional on an optional request field. `ProcessInstanceServiceImpl.queryProcessInstanceList(User, WorkflowInstanceQueryRequest)` performs `projectService.checkProjectAndAuthThrowException(...)` only inside `if (!StringUtils.isBlank(projectName))`; `ProcessDefinitionServiceImpl.filterProcessDefinition`, `TaskDefinitionServiceImpl.filterTaskDefinition` and `SchedulerServiceImpl.filterSchedules` do the same with `if (projectName != null)`. When the caller omits `projectName` (the default for a JSON body such as `{ }`, since PageQueryDto defaults pageNo/pageSize), no permission check runs at all, and the mapper queries use `<if test="projectCode != 0"> and project_code = #{projectCode}` (or no project predicate at all for schedules), so rows from every project are returned. The four v2 controllers (`/v2/workflow-instances`, `/v2/workflows/query`, `/v2/tasks/query`, `/v2/schedules/filter`) are behind only LoginHandlerInterceptor (session/API-token validity + user state); there is no @PreAuthorize, no admin-only interceptor and no role gate for /v2/** in AppConfiguration.addInterceptors.
candidates.title: Missing project authorization in v2 filter/list APIs (workflows, tasks, schedules, workflow instances) when projectName is omitted
candidates.trace: HTTP GET /v2/workflow-instances (or POST /v2/workflows/query, /v2/tasks/query, /v2/schedules/filter) -> LoginHandlerInterceptor validates session/token and user state only -> controller builds the request DTO -> service method: `projectName` is null/blank -> the `if` block containing `projectService.checkProjectAndAuthThrowException(...)` is skipped -> mapper is called with projectCode = 0/null -> mapper XML omits the `project_code` predicate (`<if test="projectCode != 0">`) -> SQL returns process definitions/task definitions/workflow instances/schedules from all projects -> records (including workflow globalParams/locations, task params, crontab, hosts, executors) are serialized back to the low-privilege caller. The same call with a projectName the user cannot access is correctly rejected, demonstrating the missing branch is the defect.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed (no code executed, no requests sent). Not verified against the upstream fix commit or any CVE/advisory mapping, so I cannot assert this is the exact regression the benchmark targets. I also did not confirm whether deployments typically restrict /v2/** at a gateway, and I did not test how the UI or API tests exercise these endpoints. A related but separate robustness defect exists at ProcessInstanceServiceImpl.java lines 410-412 (NPE when projectName is set but workflowName/process definition name does not resolve); it is not part of this candidate.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization / CWE-862 Missing Authorization

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned source snapshot (3332 files; 1723 Java). Focus areas: dolphinscheduler-api security stack (LoginHandlerInterceptor, SecurityConfig, AbstractAuthenticator, SessionServiceImpl, UsersServiceImpl), all api controllers including v1 and v2, the main service implementations (ProcessInstance/ProcessDefinition/TaskDefinition/Scheduler/Resources/Executor), DAO mapper XML for user-controlled SQL/`${}` usage, common utilities (FileUtils, JSONUtils, HttpUtils, ParameterUtils, RegexUtils), and the command/process and path sinks in alert, task and datasource plugins. The P1 relation index reports partial coverage: 3291 of 3332 source files indexed, 41 source files missing from the index, no control-flow or data-flow analysis, no semantic resolution, and only syntax/navigation relations; I treated its facts as navigation hints and verified every cited location against source text. I did not execute builds or tests and did not review the Vue UI, registry/storage plugins, or every task plugin exhaustively.
limitations: No runtime or build verification: all conclusions are from static source reading; the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed exploit.
Cannot map the finding to a specific upstream fix commit/CVE from inside the sandbox; the snapshot is the 3.2.0 tree without git history.
The v2 endpoints' practical exposure may depend on deployment (reverse proxy/gateway restrictions) that is outside the source snapshot.
The P1 relation index omits 41 source files and does not implement data-flow/control-flow or semantic resolution, so reachability and taint were reasoned manually and may miss additional paths.
Large modules (dolphinscheduler-ui, registry plugins, most storage/task plugin implementations) were sampled rather than exhaustively reviewed.
Other pre-existing weaknesses (dependency versions, the switch-task JS engine, OAuth2 flow) were noted but not exhaustively validated.

rejected_leads.lead: Switch task evaluates the user-supplied condition with the default Nashorn JS engine (dolphinscheduler-master/.../SwitchTaskUtils.java:34-37 via SwitchLogicTask.java:103-107), which allows Java interop and thus master-process RCE.
rejected_leads.reason: The docs (docs/docs/en/guide/task/switch.md:7) state expression evaluation with javax.script.ScriptEngine.eval is intended behavior, and the workflow author who sets the condition can already run shell/python tasks on workers; no source-level restriction or missing check could be shown, so this is a design/hardening concern rather than a clear vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: HttpUtils installs an all-trusting X509TrustManager (dolphinscheduler-common/.../common/utils/HttpUtils.java:86-113) used by alert/HTTP paths.
rejected_leads.reason: Pre-existing, endpoint is caller-configured (not attacker-selected in a clear trust boundary crossing) and it is not evident it was changed by any security fix; weak evidence of exploitability for this review.

rejected_leads.lead: Script alert plugin (`ScriptSender.java:87-105`) builds `/bin/sh -c` commands with title/content/userParams interpolated into single quotes.
rejected_leads.reason: The code already rejects `'` in userParams, title and content, and single quotes are the only escape from single-quoted POSIX shell context; I could not construct an injection bypass from source, so the mitigation appears adequate.

rejected_leads.lead: MySQL/OceanBase/StarRocks JDBC datasource handling of user-supplied driver properties (`autoDeserialize`, `allowLoadLocalInfile`).
rejected_leads.reason: The snapshot already contains the mitigations (APPEND_PARAMS forcing the flags to false, key filtering in transformOther, and removal of autoDeserialize from user/password in MySQL/OceanBase/StarRocks processors), so no missing check was identified there.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal via resource names/fullNames in ResourcesServiceImpl and storage operators.
rejected_leads.reason: `FileUtils.directoryTraversal` checks are present on directory name, file alias, original filename and online-create fileName paths, and the storage operators prefix tenant directories; no concrete unguarded path was found.

rejected_leads.lead: OAuth2 login flow creates a session for a provider-returned username without checking user state/tenant (`LoginController.loginByAuth2`).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires the optional `security.authentication.oauth2.enable=true` configuration plus a malicious/compromised OAuth2 provider; impact depends on unverified deployment configuration and is weaker than the confirmed missing-authorization path.

rejected_leads.lead: `SessionServiceImpl.getSession` reads the session row by ID and never checks the stored IP or last-login timeout, so a stolen sessionId is not IP-bound.
rejected_leads.reason: This matches upstream behavior in this release and the session ID is an unguessable UUID; no source evidence of a fix regression was found.

summary: Apache DolphinScheduler 3.2.0 snapshot (3332 files, 1723 Java). After reviewing the API security stack (interceptors, session/token handling), the v1/v2 controllers, the service layer's project-authorization calls, DAO mappers, and the main injection sinks in the alert/task/datasource plugins, the strongest distinct issue is a missing-authorization bug in the new v2 filter/list APIs: their service methods run project permission checks only when an optional `projectName` is supplied, and the backing mapper queries drop the project filter when `projectCode` is 0. Any authenticated user — including one with no project grants — can therefore page through workflows, task definitions, schedules and workflow instances belonging to every project. When `projectName` is present the checks do run, which shows the intended control and makes the omission in the other branch the root cause. One candidate submitted; other leads (switch-task Nashorn eval, alert-script quoting filter, MySQL JDBC `autoDeserialize`, resource path traversal, OAuth2 session creation) were checked and rejected for the reasons below.
